text:
anya: Heads-up — customer infra asked about automatic fallback when primary model is saturated. They want predictable failover by tier+region and per-tenant visibility. thinking about console UX + telemetry we need.

mike: +1. we have the routing hooks already but the missing pieces are the signals we surface and the precedence rules.

samir: proposing we treat 'saturation' as two signals: (1) in-flight queue length > N for X seconds, (2) capacity_utilization > 95% for Y sec. when both hold -> trigger soft fallback.

liz: prefer making N and Y configurable per-tenant tier. enterprise tenants may want threshold=99 and sticky routing, startup tiers want earlier diversion.

cheng: agree. also we need to ensure billing is accurate: if we fallback to smaller variant, tokens billed should reflect actual model used. console should show token delta.

anya: UX ask: show a small badge in the model dashboard: "Fallbacks: 2.3% (last 24h)" plus a chart of latency delta and cost savings. we should allow expanding to see per-tenant breakdown.

console-design: mockup idea — a compact line in the model summary with a sparkline and a hover that shows top 5 tenants affected + reason codes (queue, util, quota). can add a switch: "auto-fallback by tier" toggled per-model.

mike: question on API semantics: should we allow request-level override header like `X-Rwd-Variant-Preference` that can pin to preferred variant or disable auto-fallback for that call?

samir: yes but default must preserve platform safety. header allowed only if tenant has "variant_override" permission. otherwise platform respects tier policy.

anya: +1. permissions gating is crucial. also add telemetry event `variant_fallback` with fields: `tenant_id`, `from_model`, `to_model`, `trigger`, `latency_before`, `latency_after`, `cost_before`, `cost_after`, `sticky=true/false`.

mike: ops-bot: can you emit example log format for the event?

ops-bot: `INFO fallback event tenant=acme from=rwd-13b to=rwd-7b-quant trigger=queue_exhaustion qlen=42 util=98% latency_from=180ms latency_to=120ms cost_delta=-0.67`

liz: telemetry storage/retention question — we need fallbacks tied to evaluation prompts for regression checks. keep detailed events for 90 days, aggregate metrics for 13 months.

cheng: runtime change: when fallback occurs we should warm KV cache for the to_model if possible to avoid cold-start penalty. maybe prefetch top N keys from recent requests for that tenant. cost tradeoff but reduces latency spike.

samir: good idea. create a short circuit: if predicted benefit > cost_of_prefetch then prefetch. model-pair profile will give that estimate.

mike: rollout plan: start with a dark-launch: emit `variant_fallback_decision` events but do not actually swap. UI will display "will fallback" counts. after ~2 weeks and customer opt-in we flip on for non-critical tiers.

anya: should we add console control to set per-tenant allowed fallback variants list? e.g., allow `rwd-7b-quant` but block `rwd-3b-legacy` due to safety.

console-design: yep — list UI with allow/deny toggles + a search. also surface reasons why variant is recommended (latency/cost/compatibility).

mike: one more policy detail: precedence order: explicit request header -> tenant override list -> tenant tier policy -> region override -> global policy fallback. document this.

samir: sticky routing note: if fallback happens during a request, we should mark session sticky to `to_model` for next M minutes or until a success window, to avoid flapping. add metric `sticky_switch_count`.

liz: monitoring alerts: create alert if fallback_rate > X% for a tenant and latency_after > latency_SLO by Y ms. we should also surface when fallback causes quality regressions via our eval hooks.

anya: agreed. action items: 1) mike/samir write spec for signals + event schema; 2) console-design + liz mock telemetry panels; 3) cheng prototype KV prefetch heuristic; 4) ops: add dark-launch event emission. I'll schedule a sync next Tue.

mike: capturing now. I'll draft RFC and include sample curl that shows override header: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -H "X-Rwd-Variant-Preference: rwd-7b-quant" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"..."}'
```

samir: note: header name may change, but example is fine. also we'll add `fallback_reason_code` set to one of [queue_exhaustion, capacity_util, tenant_quota, region_unavailable].

anya: thanks all — big win if we can make fallbacks visible and controllable without breaking SLOs. :thumbsup:

liz: 👍 I'll start the mockups and link the Figma in the RFC when it's ready.

console-design: adding Figma link to RFC draft in #design later today.

cheng: will spike KV prefetch experiment on staging tomorrow.

ops-bot: Deploy job queued: `deploy/fallback-dark-launch` — status: queued.

anya: perfect. closing thread for now. keep comments in the RFC doc.
